summary: WP-007 passes code review. The ThreadPoolProgressProvisioner fake is well-designed and the 3 cross-thread success tests (OnSuccess_InvokesOnCompleteCallback, OnSuccess_AppendsLogEntries, OnSuccess_SetsMessage) provide genuine new coverage not present in the existing suite.

The 2 cancel/throw tests (WhenCancelled_DoesNotInvokeOnCompleteCallback, WhenProvisionerThrows_DoesNotInvokeOnCompleteCallback) are functional duplicates of pre-existing tests that use identical fakes. comments.note: ThreadPoolProgressProvisioner fake correctly uses `await Task.Yield()` to hop to a ThreadPool thread before reporting progress. This is the appropriate technique for genuinely exercising the cross-thread code paths in ProvisioningToolsViewModel (Log.Add dispatched via Dispatcher.UIThread.Post, direct Message assignment from ThreadPool).

3 of the 5 new tests provide genuine cross-thread coverage not present in the existing suite: StartAsync_OnSuccess_InvokesOnCompleteCallback (callback fires from ThreadPool), StartAsync_OnSuccess_AppendsLogEntries (Log populated from ThreadPool), StartAsync_OnSuccess_SetsMessage (Message set from ThreadPool). These are additive and correct.

StartAsync_WhenCancelled_DoesNotInvokeOnCompleteCallback and StartAsync_WhenProvisionerThrows_DoesNotInvokeOnCompleteCallback are functional duplicates of the pre-existing StartAsync_WhenProvisioningIsCancelled_DoesNotInvokeOnComplete and StartAsync_WhenProvisionerThrows_DoesNotInvokeOnComplete tests. Both pairs use identical fakes (BlockingProvisioner / FailingProvisioner) and differ only in variable name (callCount vs called) and assertion style. Neither new test exercises the ThreadPoolProgressProvisioner. This is test redundancy rather than cross-thread coverage. Not blocking, but a maintainability note: if the cancel/throw behaviour changes, engineers will need to update two tests instead of one.
